'''Nesin Mathematics Village''' ({{langx|tr|Nesin Matematik Köyü}}) is a [[Nonprofit organization|non-profit]] [[Educational institute|educational]] and [[research institute]] devoted to [[mathematics]]. It was founded in 2007 and is located near the village of [[Şirince]], in [[Selçuk|Selçuk district]] ([[İzmir Province]], western Turkey). 

This initiative was started by [[Ali Nesin]] and [[Sevan Nişanyan]] and generated many controversies with the [[Turkish state]] through the years. It received international recognition, and expended to others topics like [[art]] and [[philosophy]]. 

One of the main goals is to make students more active when learning. They are also involved in the daily [[Intentional community|communal]] management of the village. 

The village's logo is a [[rooster]], described by Ali Nesin as an "animal that wakes you up, enlightens you".<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Yam |first=Philip |date=2018-08-09 |title=Ali Nesin: Fighter for Math’s Next Generation |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2018/08/09/a-fighter-for-maths-next-generation/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=[[Simons Foundation]] |language=en-US}}</ref> 

==History==

=== Origins ===
[[Ali Nesin]] is a Turkish mathematician specialized in [[algebra]] and its interplay with [[Mathematical logic|logic]]. He's the son of [[Aziz Nesin]], a famous Turkish writer and [[Satire|satirist]] whose [[Atheism in Turkey|atheism]] attracted controversy. At the death of his father, in 1995, Ali Nesin gave up his research position in the [[USA]] to return in Turkey and take over the {{Interlanguage link|Nesin Foundation|tr|Nesin Vakfı}}, a [[charitable organization]] created by Aziz Nesin to support and educate [[Child poverty|disadvantaged children]].<ref name=":3" />

In 1996, Ali Nesin became the head of the mathematics [[Academic department|department]] of the newly founded [[Istanbul Bilgi University]]. He lead an ambitious program, where first-year students were taught [[axiomatic set theory]], including concepts like [[Ordinals (mathematics)|ordinals]], [[Cardinal (mathematics)|cardinals]], the [[axiom of choice]], [[Zorn's lemma|Zorn’s lemma]] and [[Non-standard model of arithmetic|nonstandard numbers]].<ref name=":1" /> However, many students were struggling.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Padavic-Callaghan |first=Karmela |date=7 January 2026 |title=These images explore a ‘utopic’ village built for teaching maths |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2510019-these-images-explore-a-utopic-village-built-for-teaching-maths/ |website=[[New Scientist]]}}</ref> In 1998, he started organizing [[Summer school|summer schools]] to fill up the knowledge gaps; but despite the help from the university, the logistic organization was too complicated to go on.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Aslı Rino Nesin|first=Gabriela|date=April 2016|title=Le Village Nesin des mathématiques en Turquie|url=https://smf.emath.fr/system/files/filepdf/Nesin-bd.pdf|journal=Gazette de la SMF|language=fr|issue=148}}</ref> 

Together with his friend [[Sevan Nişanyan]], a subversive writer and architect, they dreamed of a mathematical village. As Nişanyan recalls: <blockquote>"We used to talk […] about the ideal educational environment, the architecture, the setting, the operation and so on. We looked […] at medieval [[monasteries]] and old Turkish [[medreses]]. And then one day, all of a sudden, it started looking doable."<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Karaali |first=Gizem |date=June 2014 |title=Nesin Math Village: Mathematics as a Revolutionary Act |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00283-014-9453-5 |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |language=en |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=45–49 |doi=10.1007/s00283-014-9453-5 |issn=0343-6993|url-access=subscription }}</ref></blockquote>They made the construction plans, and the building started in {{Date|spring 2007}} on a one hectare land located {{cvt|800|m}} from [[Şirince]], a town where Nişanyan previously restored buildings. The same year, around 100 students came (mostly from [[Istanbul Bilgi University]]) for the first summer school. Students and teachers helped for the construction.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":2" />

=== Legal issues ===

==== Village eviction of 2007 ====
{{Wikinews|Mathematics summer school in Turkey threatened by authorities}}
[[File:Blackboard under arrest Lenta3-small-797574.jpg|thumb|A [[blackboard]] of the village cordoned off by [[police tape]], in 2007.]]
Many places around [[Şirince]] are [[Protected area|protected areas]], but the village is not; still, the [[construction permit]] was not granted. Reasons given for the refusal are the absence of officially registered "street", and the interdiction to build an [[educational institution]] without the government approval. Another suspected reason is the controversiality of the name "Nesin", dating back from the figure of [[Aziz Nesin]]. In {{Date|July 2007}}, everyone was forced out of the village by the [[Jandarma]], who came with guns drawn and sealed off buildings.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last=Greuel |first=Gert-Martin |url=https://doi.org/10.1142/11060 |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM 2018) |date=2018-06-06 |publisher=[[World Scientific]] |year=2018 |isbn=978-981-327-287-3 |volume=1 |chapter=Ali Nesin and the Nesin Mathematical Village |doi=10.1142/9789813272880_0002}}</ref> The villagers, representing three [[dozen]] people, camped in the nearby woods, which are a former [[horse burial]] place filled with [[Horse bone|bones]]. Courses continued outdoor, but the Jandarma tried to force them out again. [[Ali Nesin]], who previously tried to keep the project secret because of its illegality, decided to send his personal diary about the school to the journal ''[[Radikal]]''.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Nesin |first=Ali |author-link=Ali Nesin |date=7 August 2007 |title=Kur bir matematik köyü gör başına neler gelir! |trans-title=Just try visiting a math village and see what happens to you! |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080121205203/https://www.radikal.com.tr/haber.php?haberno=229185 |access-date=26 August 2026 |work=[[Radikal]]}}</ref> A letter of complaint was written by the mathematician [[Alexandre Borovik]] (who was teaching there), signed by 384 scholars and sent to [[Prime Minister of Turkey|prime minister]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]].<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Borovik |first=Alexandre |author-link=Alexandre Borovik |date=2007-08-03 |title=Letter to His Excellency Recep Tayyip Erdogan |url=https://savesummerschool.blogspot.com/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=Save Mathematical Summer School}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=August 9, 2007 |title=Scientists react to the shutting down of mathematics school (RADİKAL) |url=http://www.turkishdailynews.com.tr/article.php?enewsid=80402 |work=[[Hürriyet Daily News]]}}</ref> The village reopened on the {{Date|10th of August, 2007}}.<ref name=":10" /> This publicity brought popular support and donations.<ref name=":9" /> 

Ali Nesin got sued by the state for illegal construction and illegally creating an educational institution. He was acquitted for the first case, and the second one was not settled as of 2019.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Berlioux |first=Jeremie |date=23 January 2019 |title=Turkey's 'Mathematics Village': Changing education, one equation at a time |url=https://www.middleeasteye.net/features/turkeys-mathematics-village-changing-education-one-equation-time |access-date=2026-08-24 |work=[[Middle East Eye]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== Demolition scare ====
According to a statement in July 2017 by Tekin Karadağ, the president of the Şirince Environment and Nature Association, Nesin Mathematics Village was slated for demolition by the authorities as being an "illegal construction".<ref>{{cite news|title=Şirince'de yıkım başlıyor|trans-title=Demolition begins in Şirince|author=Banu Şen|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sirincede-yikim-basliyor-40536452|newspaper=[[Hürriyet]]|date=31 July 2017|access-date=31 July 2017}}</ref> However, Harun Abuş, Director of Development and City Planning of Selçuk Municipality, declared that at this moment Nesin Mathematics Village is "not on the demolition calendar".<ref>{{cite news|title="Şirince'deki Matematik Köyü ve Nişanyan Evleri, yıkım takviminde yok"|trans-title="Mathematics Village and Nişanyan Houses in Şirince not on the demolition calendar"|url=http://t24.com.tr/haber/sirincedeki-matematik-koyu-ve-nisanyan-evleri-yikim-takvimde-yok,417504|newspaper=T24|date=1 August 2017|access-date=4 August 2017}}</ref>

=== Other villages ===

The Nesin Mathematical Village is still expanding, mostly to build more dormitories but also to host sister villages about [[philosophy]] and [[art]].<ref name=":2" /> In 2014, when talking about this expansion, [[Ali Nesin]] stated that <blockquote>"the whole valley should be dedicated to education, not a standard one but a 'pirate' one".<ref name=":6" /></blockquote>In 2013, the village was extended to host the Nesin Philosophy Village, and summer schools started in 2014.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Eşkinat |first=Rana |url=https://www.asecu.gr/files/12th_conf_proceedings.pdf |title=Proceedings of the 12th International Conference of ASECU: Inclusive and Sustainable Development and the Role of Social and Solidarity Economy |last2=Tepecik |first2=Filiz |year=2016 |isbn=978-975-06-2040-9 |pages=170 |language=en |format=PDF}}</ref> Since the same year, it also hosts the Nesin Art Village, founded by [[Işın Önol]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=Dec 13, 2016 |title=The Nesin Mathematics Village: a Dream to Think, Learn and Enjoy Math |url=https://interestingengineering.com/innovation/nesin-mathematics-village-learn-enjoy-math |access-date=August 24, 2024 |work=Interesting Engineering}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kiger |first=Rumeysa |date=August 30, 2015 |title=Art follows in the footsteps of math in Şirince village |url=http://www.todayszaman.com/arts-culture_art-follows-in-the-footsteps-of-math-in-sirince-village_397834.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118081949/http://www.todayszaman.com/arts-culture_art-follows-in-the-footsteps-of-math-in-sirince-village_397834.html |archive-date=January 18, 2016 |access-date=August 24, 2024 |work=Today's Zaman}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kocal |first=Ece |date=October 16, 2015 |title=Matematik Köyü'nün Artık Bir Kardeşi Var: Sanat Köyü |trans-title=Mathematics Village Now Has a Sibling: The Art Village |url=https://www.artfulliving.com.tr/sanat/matematik-koyunun-artik-bir-kardesi-var-sanat-koyu-i-3555 |access-date=August 28, 2024 |work=Artful Living |language=tr}}</ref>

== Architecture ==
Buildings are mainly made of blocks of stones sealed with a mix of [[hay]] and [[clay]], and sometimes of recycled materials (like old [[Railway track#Rail|train rails]] and [[Railroad tie|ties]]). Trees and [[virginia creeper]] were planted to provide shadow.<ref name=":2" /> Many dogs and cats are roaming free.<ref name=":7" /> 

As of 2018, the village's territory represents 35,000m², half of it being covered by [[olive trees]]. There are sixteen bedrooms, two amphitheaters, four closed and four open-air lecture halls, a library, two [[Turkish baths]], twenty-nine single or double rooms, a kitchen, a cafeteria, a small shop and an [[observation tower]].<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":8" /> There is no computer room, as the village tries to nurture student cooperation and avoid distractions.<ref name=":7" />

As of 2019, the village can host up to 500 students.<ref name=":8" /> Most of them sleep in [[Tent|tents]], as dormitories are not sufficient.<ref name=":2" />

=== Particular buildings ===
[[File:Classroom in Nesin Matematik Köyü.jpg|thumb|A covered amphitheater.]]
The first classroom to be built is called the "Langlands shed", named in honor of [[Robert Langlands]]. He donated a portion of the his [[Shaw Prize]] (awarded in 2007) to the village, and did it again when receiving the [[Abel Prize]] (2018).<ref name=":6" />

The "[[Sevan Nişanyan]] Library" opened its doors on June 15, 2013.<ref name=":3" /> It consists of a 150 seats conference room on the ground floor, and [[Mezzanine|mezzanines]] on the first floor where most of the 15.000 books are stored. It is furnished mostly with donations.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":2" /> 

== Functioning ==

=== Logistic organization ===
The village operates on the [[Intentional community|commune]] model. Students usually stay in the village for two weeks, and aside from following courses they have to accomplish [[Housekeeping|chores]] (cleaning, helping the cook, dishwashing, gardening...), most of them being done after lunch.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karakurt |first=Altuğ |date=2014-08-21 |title=An ordinary day in Turkey’s 'Mathematics Village' |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/an-ordinary-day-in-turkeys-mathematics-village-70755 |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref> They are organized in groups mixing high school and university students.<ref name=":1" /> There is always a student who previously came to the village, and explains the tasks to their groupmates. There is no "supervisor", as the system relies on mutual trust.<ref name=":0" /> This provides a sense of [[collective ownership]] and [[community]].<ref name=":7" />

High school students, who are usually [[Minor (law)|minors]], are placed under the responsibility of a "big brother or sister" who is usually a volunteering university student.<ref name=":1" />

Each Thursday, a vacation activity is organized (usually a visit to [[Ephesus]] or a boat tour). There are no TVs, broadcast music nor swimming pool, in order to "protect the village from factors which could be detrimental to concentration". Still, there are ping-pong tables and it is common for students to play live music (usually [[guitar]], [[Bağlama|saz]] or [[Kemenche|kemençe]]) on the evening, or to project a movie.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":7">{{Citation |last=Emre-Akdoğan |first=Elçin |title=Ancient School Without Walls: Collective Creativity in the Mathematics Village |date=2018 |work=Mathematics Education in the Digital Era |pages=413–437 |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-72381-5_17 |access-date=2026-08-22 |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-72379-2 |last2=Yazgan-Sağ |first2=Gönül}}</ref>

Around fifteen paid staff and nearly one hundred volunteers work there every year.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Krishnaswami Alladi and Gabriela Asli Rino Nesin|year=2015|title=The Nesin Mathematics Village in Turkey|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201506/rnoti-p652.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=62-6|pages=652–658}}</ref> A [[chef]] supervises three meals a day, plus cake in the afternoon.<ref name=":2" />

=== Economic model ===
The Mathematics Village is a [[Nonprofit organization|non-profit organization]]. There is a "[[pay what you can]]" fee for attending [[Summer school|summer schools]],<ref name=":5" /> but there is also an "unquestionable policy" to never refuse anyone for economic reasons,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/haber-detay.aspx?pageID=238&nid=70193|title=A brief introduction to Turkey's 'Mathematics Village|website=Hürriyet Daily News|date=9 August 2014 |access-date=2017-03-26|last=Karakurt|first=Altuğ}}</ref> hence the {{Interlanguage link|Nesin Foundation|tr|Nesin Vakfı}} provides grants.<ref name=":8" />

Teaching is voluntary. Instructors don't receive an [[Honorarium|honoraria]], but the village provides free accommodations and meals. Thematic summer schools are also the occasion for researchers to collaborate outside of their lecture time.<ref name=":1" />

The village is funded by donations made to the {{Interlanguage link|Nesin Foundation|tr|Nesin Vakfı}}. The names of donors (mostly [[Physical person|physical persons]]) are listed on the walls of a building.<ref name=":8" /> Another source of money is the local production of olives and oil. The village receives no funding from the [[Turkish state]], but it occasionally does from research institutes (like the [[TÜBİTAK]]).<ref name=":5" />

== Mathematical activities ==
[[File:Matematik Köyü Ali Nesin Ders Anlatırken 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Ali Nesin]] teaching at the village in 2007.]]The original teaching intention of [[Ali Nesin]] is to make students active in class. He sums up this goal for autonomy by the moto: "don't look for the answer, look for truth".<ref name=":5">{{Citation |last=Pelek |first=Selin |title=Tentatives pour reconstruire le champ éducatif : les initiatives d’éducation alternative en Turquie |date=2024-12-12 |work=L’économie solidaire entre un mouvement par le bas et sa reconnaissance internationale |pages=105–117 |url=https://shs.cairn.info/article/AGRAPH_GAJA_2024_01_0105 |access-date=2026-08-21 |publisher=Éditions Sociographe |language=fr |isbn=978-2-494241-22-0}}</ref> This is put in opposition with regular [[Turkish education system|Turkish schools]], which are supposedly more focus on [[memorization]].<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />

=== Audience ===
The target audience initially consisted of university and [[PhD student|PhD students]], but it quickly included any education level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jozuka |first=Emiko |date=2016-02-25 |title=Welcome to the Turkish ‘Village’ Dedicated to Maths |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/welcome-to-the-turkish-village-dedicated-to-maths/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Many applications are refused due to the lack of space.<ref name=":8" /> In 2017, the village was visited by 10,379 children of the age of 13 or older.<ref name=":6" />

The village also hosts domestic and international research events,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://matematikkoyu.org/eng/events.php|title=Events {{!}} Nesin Mathematics Village|last=nesinvakfi.org|first=Nesin Vakfı|website=matematikkoyu.org|language=tr|access-date=2017-03-26|archive-date=2017-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326231241/http://matematikkoyu.org/eng/events.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> and research papers are written there.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nesin Köyleri {{!}} Akademik Makalelerde Matematik Köyü/Academic Articles from the Maths Village |url=https://nesinkoyleri.org/akademik-makalelerde-matematik-koyu/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Borovik |first=Alexandre V. |title=Economy of Thought: A Neglected Principle of Mathematics Education |date=2017 |work=Mathematics, Culture, and the Arts |pages=239–265 |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-53385-8_18 |access-date=2026-08-26 |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-53383-4 |author-link=Alexandre Borovik}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

=== Content ===
Most of the teaching activity consists in [[Summer school|summer schools]]. Courses span between 6 and 8 hours of the day, and range from high school to graduate university courses. All high school courses are taught in [[Turkish language|Turkish]], as the students do not necessarily know foreign languages, but any [[Undergraduate education|undergraduate]] or [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] course may be taught in English. Informal seminars are sometimes held between 9 and 11 p.m. in the "[[Aziz Nesin]] Amphitheater".<ref name=":1" /> There are no exams nor diplomas delivered.<ref name=":2" />

Many courses are filmed and accessible online,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matematik Ders Videoları/Mathematics Lecture Videos |url=https://nesinkoyleri.org/matematik-ders-videolari/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=Nesin Köyleri |language=tr-TR}}</ref> in more than 7,000 videos. In 2010, the [[Turkish Mathematical Society]] awarded [[Ali Nesin]] a prize for his [[open source]] courseware.<ref name=":6" />  

Students have reported to appreciate their experience at the village for its distinct approach on instruction, the nurturing of curiosity, the natural environment and the cohabitation with mathematicians.<ref name=":7" />

== Recognition ==
In 2015, [[Ali Nesin]] received the 14th "{{Interlanguage link|Koç Award for education|tr|Vehbi Koç Ödülü}}" from the [[Vehbi Koç Foundation]], for his work at the Nesin Mathematics Village.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2015 |title=The winners of the 14th Vehbi Koç Award for Education are Professor Ali Nesin and the Mathematics Village Project. |url=https://www.vehbikocodulu.com/odul-alanlar/2015/ali-nesin/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=Vehbi Koç Ödülü |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-02-26 |title=Turkish founder of Mathematics Village honored with Koç award - Türkiye News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-founder-of-mathematics-village-honored-with-koc-award-78931 |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=[[Hürriyet Daily News]] |language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Ali Nesin and Sevan Nishanyan ICM 2018 (43216381614).jpg|thumb|Ali Nesin and [[Sevan Nişanyan]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] 2018, with a picture of the village library behind them.]]

In 2018, Ali Nesin was bestowed the [[Leelavati Award]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (hosted in [[Rio de Janeiro]])<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ghys |first=Etienne |author-link=Étienne Ghys |date=2018-09-27 |title=L’aventure d’un village mathématique |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2018/09/26/l-aventure-d-un-village-mathematique_5360595_1650684.html |access-date=2026-08-25 |work=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr |issn=1950-6244}}</ref> for<blockquote>"his outstanding contributions towards increasing public awareness of mathematics in Turkey, in particular for his tireless work in creating the 'Mathematical Village' as an exceptional, peaceful place for education, research, and the exploration of mathematics for anyone."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/leelavati-prize/leelavati-prize-2018|title=Leelavati Prize 2018 {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=mathunion.org|access-date=2018-08-04}}</ref></blockquote>
